newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aides said to obtain FBI files despite mistake.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aides said to obtain FBI files despite mistake.

text.p: The Clinton White House obtained FBI files on Republicans including former Secretary of State James Baker even after aides learned such files should not be obtained, according to Senate documents released on Friday.

Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Orrin Hatch said the information showed FBI files on hundreds of former Republican officials and aides were not obtained in a bureaucratic snafu as President Clinton has said.

"My feeling is that somebody (at the White Houwe) wanted to find dirt on these people either for current uses or uses at some time in the future," Hatch said. "But to conclusively prove that at this point, we haven't been able to."
The White House accused Hatch of playing politics five weeks before the U.S. presidential election and said the Senate investigation proved no wrong-doing.
"Despite Mr. Hatch's partisan stunt, the bottom line remains clear: There is no indication that any FBI files were misused," White House aide Mark Fabiani said.

The new information includes a sworn statement to Hatch's committee investigators by former White House aide Mari Anderson saying the White House office that obtained the files learned around September 1993 that the Republicans no longer had White House passes so there was no need to see their FBI security files.

Hatch, a Utah Republican, said Anderson also told the committee someone removed six months of pages from a log of White House officials who looked at the files, Hatch said. Though she could not remember their looking at files of former Republican officials, she could not recollect for certain whether they did, he added.

Anderson said the White House Office of Personnel Security aides who learned of the mistaken lists included Anthony Marceca, the aide in charge of obtaining the FBI files. She said Marceca then painstakingly went through Secret Service lists to try to determine which names on them should be crossed off because the people listed no longer had White House passes.

But the Senate committee said the White House office obtained FBI files of half a dozen well-known Republican officials after September 1993. It said they included Baker, former White House press secretary Marlin Fitzwater and Tony Blankley, who is House Speaker Newt Gingrich's press secretary.
"According to Ms. Anderson, Marceca knew these files should not be requested," said a Senate Judiciary Committee investigators' summary released by Hatch.
